title: Flood years

data.source: USGS National Water Information System, annual peak streamflow at eight gauges (01646500, 01570500, 02035000, 03335500, 05464500, 05054000, 06191500, 11532500)

prediction: If a basin counted toward its floods, the waits between flood years would be more even than shuffled years in at least 5 of 8 rivers (P1), and the seed rule would predict next year's peak better than the running mean in at least 6 of 8 (P2). We expected both to fail.
baseline: Shuffled years (each year a fresh draw, the standard flood-frequency model); the running mean; persistence.
why: Flood years were spaced no more evenly than shuffled years, and a memory of past peaks did not beat the plain average. A river is never "due". Each year is a fresh draw, as the hydrologists say.
